RESEARCH ONLY. Do not write any files or code. Return findings as your final message text. Use WebFetch/WebSearch and curl via Bash. Cite a URL for every factual claim. QUOTE exact clauses verbatim where asked.

Context: a game-server HOSTING company is building a mod/plugin catalog + one-click server-side installer. Two sources to research in depth:

=== PART 1: CurseForge "Eternal" API ===
Docs: https://docs.curseforge.com (and https://docs.curseforge.com/rest-api/ , https://console.curseforge.com )
Report:
(a) Exact base URL (api.curseforge.com), auth header name (x-api-key), how to get a key (console.curseforge.com), whether keys are free, and any approval/commercial-use gate.
(b) Core endpoints with paths and key query params: GET /v1/games, GET /v1/categories, GET /v1/mods/search (gameId, classId, categoryId, gameVersion, searchFilter, sortField, sortOrder, modLoaderType, index, pageSize — and the 10,000 result pagination cap), GET /v1/mods/{modId}, POST /v1/mods (bulk), GET /v1/mods/{modId}/files, GET /v1/mods/{modId}/files/{fileId}, GET /v1/mods/{modId}/files/{fileId}/download-url, GET /v1/fingerprints, GET /v1/minecraft/version, GET /v1/mods/{modId}/description.
(c) Response field list for a Mod object — ESPECIALLY: logo (thumbnailUrl/url), screenshots, categories, links (websiteUrl, wikiUrl, issuesUrl, sourceUrl), downloadCount, latestFiles, allowModDistribution, authors, dateModified, classId, gameId, isAvailable. Does CurseForge expose a LICENSE field at all? (I believe it does NOT in the API — verify and say so explicitly.) Where is license shown on the website?
(d) The allowModDistribution=false / downloadUrl=null problem. Explain exactly: what it means, roughly what share of mods it affects, what third-party launchers do about it (Prism Launcher, ATLauncher, modpack installers), and what it means for a hosting company that wants to auto-install mods. Cite real sources (GitHub issues, Prism Launcher docs, CurseForge blog/announcement about third-party distribution opt-out from 2022).
(e) Known CDN URL pattern (edge.forgecdn.net / mediafilez.forgecdn.net) and whether constructing download URLs manually from fileId is allowed/works. Note: the user reports their API key gets 403 with empty body at the CDN edge — investigate whether Cloudflare blocks datacenter IPs, whether a User-Agent is required, and any documented requirements (Overwolf requires a descriptive User-Agent?). Report anything you find on 403 causes.
(f) Rate limits — what are they, documented or observed?
(g) LEGAL: QUOTE the relevant clauses from CurseForge / Overwolf Terms of Service and the CurseForge API terms about third-party applications, caching metadata, redistributing files, and commercial use. URLs: https://www.curseforge.com/legal/terms , https://www.overwolf.com/legal/terms/ , https://support.curseforge.com , any "API Terms" page. Also the CurseForge author-facing rules about third-party distribution.

=== PART 2: Nexus Mods API ===
(a) Public API v1: base URL https://api.nexusmods.com/v1/ , docs at https://app.nexusmods.com/api/docs (or https://api.nexusmods.com/ ). Auth (apikey header, personal API key from user account settings; also OAuth for apps). Endpoints: /v1/games.json, /v1/games/{game_domain_name}.json, /v1/games/{domain}/mods/{id}.json, /mods/latest_added.json, /mods/trending.json, /mods/{id}/files.json, and the download-link endpoint /v1/games/{domain}/mods/{id}/files/{file_id}/download_link.json.
(b) CRITICAL: is the download_link endpoint restricted to Premium users only? Quote the docs. What about the nxm:// link + key/expires params for non-premium?
(c) Rate limits (X-RL-Daily-Limit / Hourly headers, 2500/day 100/hour figures) — cite.
(d) Is there a newer GraphQL API (api.nexusmods.com/v2/graphql)? Detail what is known/public.
(e) LEGAL — QUOTE clauses from https://help.nexusmods.com/article/18-api-acceptable-use-policy (API Acceptable Use Policy) and Nexus Mods Terms of Service https://help.nexusmods.com/article/. Especially anything about: automated downloads, redistribution, mirroring, caching, commercial use, and whether a hosting company can download mods on a user's behalf. Nexus is known to be strict — quote it precisely.
(f) Practical verdict: is Nexus usable as a source for a commercial hosting platform's auto-installer? Say clearly yes/no/ambiguous with the quoted basis.

Be thorough. Be explicit about what you could and could not verify.

Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever any such runtime behavior would make an artifact more useful, before writing the page.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").

## Base URL
`https://api.curseforge.com`

**Header Name:** `x-api-key`

Interested parties must apply via a separate form, and "Any registered account which is not a game developer and did not request a key, will be deleted."

The documentation includes a "CurseForge for Studios Terms of Use" section but does not provide the full text within this page.

Based on the search results, here's what I found regarding CurseForge API and its impact on third-party launchers:

## The Key Issue

CurseForge introduced a toggle that enables creators to choose whether or not they want to allow distribution of their mods outside of the CurseForge ecosystem. When creators set `allowModDistribution` to false and `downloadUrl` becomes null, it prevents third-party launchers from accessing those mods.

## Impact on Third-Party Launchers

When CurseForge released the official API on May 16, 2022, this resulted in third-party launchers no longer being able to download modpacks, like MultiMC and PCL2. With the new CurseForge REST API rollout, mods are currently only accessible using the CurseForge site and the CurseForge app.

## The Reasoning

Downloads originated from 3rd party services rely on CurseForge servers and CDN, incurring substantial costs and bypassing monetization which is used to fuel the Authors Rewards Points system.

CurseForge has been trying to block 3rd party launchers from downloading "disabled" mods (creators can explicitly disallow downloads not from the website or the 1st party launcher).

**What Changed:**
The endpoint remains unchanged at `https://edge.forgecdn.net/files/{id}/{subId}/{filename}`, but authentication is now supported and will become mandatory.

- "During the current phase, the key is optional, and unauthenticated downloads keep working as before."

**CDN & Third-Party Distribution:**
The change applies to developers of "launchers, modpack installers, server tools, and similar integrations" downloading from the CurseForge CDN.

**Two Authentication Methods:**
1. Header method (recommended): `x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY`

**No allowModDistribution or User-Agent Requirements Mentioned:**
The announcement does not address these topics or specify rate limits.

**Timeline:**
- Now: Optional phase
- July 16th: Required enforcement phase with 401 error responses for unauthenticated requests

**Purpose:**
This enables attribution of downloads to their source platform, providing mod authors with better analytics about where their content originates.

• Authenticating lets us attribute downloads to your platform, giving mod authors accurate source analytics and crediting the traffic your tool delivers.
• Recommended: add your key now during the optional window so nothing breaks for your users later.
 Who this is for?
 This is aimed at the developers and operators of any tool or service that downloads files from the CurseForge CDN: launchers, modpack installers, server tools, and similar integrations.
 If you only use the CurseForge app or website, there's nothing to do here. This is handled for you.
 What's changing?
 The endpoint itself stays the same:
 https://edge.forgecdn.net/files/{id}/{subId}/{filename}
 What's new is that you can now include an API key with your request. During the current phase, the key is optional, and unauthenticated downloads keep working as before. On July 16th, a valid key will be required, and any request without one will be rejected.
 Why we're doing this?
 This change will get us a step closer towards an improved analytics system for our mod authors. It's meant to give authors a clearer understanding of where their downloads are coming from, among other important information.
 This is about attribution and analytics for creators, not gatekeeping content.
 When a file is pulled directly from the CDN today, mod authors often can't tell which tool or platform delivered the download. By having each integration authenticate with its own key, we can attribute downloads to their source and give authors a much clearer picture of where and how their work is being used.
 There's an upside for you, too: the downloads your platform delivers get credited to your platform. Instead of that traffic disappearing into an anonymous pool, authors can see the value your launcher or service brings to their content.
 How to authenticate?
 You can provide your API key in one of two ways. Both are valid, so pick whichever fits your setup.
 Option 1: Request header (recommended)
 Send your key in the x-api-key header. This is the preferred method for production, since it keeps the key out of server logs, browser history, and referrer headers.
 GET https://edge.forgecdn.net/files/1234/56/ExampleMod-2.0-1.20.1.jar
x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY
 curl:
 curl "https://edge.forgecdn.net/files/1234/56/ExampleMod-2.0-1.20.1.jar" \
  --output ExampleMod.jar
 JavaScript (fetch):
 const response = await fetch( "https://edge.forgecdn.net/files/1234/56/ExampleMod-2.0-1.20.1.jar", { headers: { "x-api-key": "YOUR_API_KEY" } });
 Python (requests):
 import requestsurl = "https://edge.forgecdn.net/files/1234/56/ExampleMod-2.0-1.20.1.jar"headers = {"x-api-key": "YOUR_API_KEY"}response = requests.get(url, headers=headers)response.raise_for_status()with open("ExampleMod-2.0-1.20.1.jar", "wb") as f: f.write(response.content)
 Option 2: Query parameter
 Append ?api-key=YOUR_API_KEY to any CDN URL. Handy for quick tests in a browser or with curl:
 curl "https://edge.forgecdn.net/files/1234/56/ExampleMod-2.0-1.20.1.jar?api-key=YOUR_API_KEY" \ -o ExampleMod-2.0-1.20.1.jar
 Note: Query parameters can show up in server access logs and browser history. Prefer the header method anywhere it matters.
 Timeline
 Phase: Now
Behavior: API key accepted but optional. Unauthenticated requests still succeed.
 Phase: Future (July 16th)
Behavior: API key required. Requests without a valid key return 401 Unauthorized.
 What a rejected request looks like
 Once enforcement is active, requests without a valid key will return an error:
 HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized{ "error": "Unauthorized", "message": "A valid api-key is required."}
 Build for this now: handle 401 responses gracefully and surface a clear, actionable message rather than failing silently.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about Prism Launcher, CurseForge, and the `allowModDistribution` setting regarding third-party downloads:

## Overview

The CurseForge API is restricted, and individual authors can disable third-party downloads for their projects. This restriction is controlled by a toggle that mod authors can set.

## How It Works

Authors can choose whether or not they want to allow distribution of their mods outside of the CurseForge ecosystem. Downloads originated from 3rd party services rely on CurseForge servers and CDN, incurring substantial costs and bypassing monetization which is used to fuel the Authors Rewards Points system.

## Prism Launcher's Handling

When Prism Launcher encounters CurseForge mods that cannot be automatically downloaded using API, it will create a download link for every such mod, and as you go, it will detect the mods in your Downloads folder and copy them to the appropriate location.

When that happens, the pack install stops and asks you to fetch those specific files by hand from the project page, then drop them into the instance. It is not a Prism bug and there is no setting that fixes it.

The search results contain GitHub issues showing that users have reported problems with handling these blocked mods, but the behavior appears to be a limitation of CurseForge's API restrictions rather than a bug with Prism Launcher itself.

Project Distribution Toggle
 Project Distribution Toggle
 Modified on: Thu, 31 Oct, 2024 at 11:21 AM
 The project distribution toggle is all about providing authors control over their intellectual property and revenue generated from their awesome creations.
 The toggle is part of the new CurseForge API, and determines if 3rd party developers can or cannot distribute your project information and files.
 What does this mean for authors? In short - each project owner can choose if the project can be distributed over 3rd party services. 
 It's important you are aware of 2 things:
 If you turn this option off Any 3rd-party service, website or client will not have access to your projects or files via the 3rd-party API.
 If you turn this option on any download from the 3rd party service will not count towards your total downloads nor towards your Reward Program earnings. How can I manage my distribution preferences? Easy - at first we're going to prompt all project owners when entering an existing project. Simply click the 'Go to License Tab' button and you'll be transferred to the relevant tab. 
 You can also edit this toggle by entering the project page > 'License tab'.
 Once there, you can view or change the distribution setting. Don't forget to hit 'Save' when you're done! You can always change your choice later on. As a default, all existing projects have the option toggled on and allow distribution.
 What about new projects? We're adding the toggle setting in the submission panel as well ('Create a Project' page), where you can determine an initial choice for the project.
 We recommend choosing a license preference that is compatible with your distribution choice. In any case - the API will respect the toggle choice over the license type choice. You will need to choose when creating your project if to turn this toggle on or off.
 I'm not the project owner - do I have access to the toggle as well? Only project owners and members with the 'license' permission enabled can view the License tab when over-viewing a project.

content.content:
# CurseForge API Key and Download Requirements

## API Key Requirements

The documentation states: "A CurseForge API key is *now* included by this image on Java 17 and newer; however, you can always supply your own instead."

To obtain a key, users should "Go to their [developer console](https://console.curseforge.com/), generate an API key, and set the environment variable `CF_API_KEY`."

However, note that "The `java8` image (and other pre-Java 17 tags) does **not** include that key."

## Manual Downloads for Restricted Content

The system accommodates mods and modpacks that prohibit automated retrieval. As documented: "For mod, modpacks, and world files that are not allowed for automated download, the container path `/downloads` can be attached and matching files will be retrieved from there."

The process involves:
- Using a browser to download restricted files from their respective pages
- Placing files in a designated directory structure
- Mounting this directory to the container's `/downloads` path

The guide emphasizes: "It's important to use a browser to download the files listed for manual download."

## Rate Limiting

The documentation does not mention rate limiting concerns or restrictions related to the CurseForge API.

# Summary of CurseForge Mod Download Issue

## Key Problem
Prism Launcher exhibits unpredictable behavior when attempting to download mods from CurseForge that have third-party downloads disabled.

## Specific Issues Documented

**Inconsistent version display:**
> "Version Select drop-down shows 'No valid version found!'"

**Silent failure scenario:** Sometimes available versions appear selectable, but downloads fail silently without error messages. The mod then appears in the mod list without actually being downloaded.

## Technical Details
- **Reported in:** Prism Launcher 6.0 with Qt 6.4.1
- **Test case:** "Save Your Pets" mod for 1.18.2 Forge instance
- **Root cause identified:** The issue notes this specific use-case lacks proper handling in the codebase

## Suggested Solutions
The issue proposer recommended:
1. Add labels indicating manual download requirement
2. Implement a dialog mechanism similar to pack downloading for affected mods

**Note:** No percentages or statistical data appear in this GitHub issue report.

 API Acceptable Use Policy
 This Acceptable Use Policy (AUP) covers the use of the Nexus Mods API in all third party websites, applications or other use cases.  Personal API keys 
 All users have the ability to generate a Personal API key, from the API Access page . This is intended to allow users to experiment with our API without using the keys assigned to a registered application. 
 We tolerate the use of your personal API key with applications that are in the testing stage of development or are intended for personal use only. Please note that as soon as a public-facing application has left the testing stage and is intended to be utilised by a wider audience (i.e. end-users rather than a select group of testers) you should contact support@nexusmods.com to register your application as described in the registration process in this document.

 Registration process 
 In cases where your application is intended to be public-facing, we require you to contact the Nexus Mods support team once you have a testing build of the application which demonstrates the intended usage of our API. This will allow us to ensure not only that your application complies with this policy, but that it further does not consume an excess amount of API requests (which may result in users being rate limited ).
 In order to get your application registered, please follow these simple steps:
 Contact our support team ( support@nexusmods.com ) and include a testing build of your application which can be used with a personal API key. 
 Make any necessary changes to your application, then send us a name, short description and logo for your application. This will be displayed on the API Access page. All logos should be reasonably high resolution and be visible when displayed on a dark background. 
 Your application will then be issued a "slug" for use with the SSO.
 Registered applications are listed on the API Access page accessible via the site preferences. Users have the ability to revoke the API key issued to your application at any time. 
 Once your application has been registered you will be able to take advantage of our Single Sign-On (SSO) system . Although this is not a requirement, it is the most convenient way for users to add their API key to your application.
 Please note that us registering an application does not imply an endorsement of the application, nor do we take any responsibility for the application functioning as intended. 
 API access and open source 
 In the spirit of fostering cooperation between developers and in the modding community in general, we provide an open API and we release all of our software and tools as open source. 
 Therefore, we strongly encourage any applications using our API to make use of open-source licensing, too. We reserve the right to deny registration to any applications if we have doubts about the nature of the application itself, the way our data and our users’ data is handled, or that the underlying code is fully complying with this policy.
 Including the source code with your registration request will allow us to gain a better understanding of your application's intended purpose and may speed up the registration process.
 Request Headers 
 When sending requests to the Nexus Mods API, we ask that you add appropriate information to the request header which identifies your application. Specifically including these fields:
 Application-Version (e.g. "1.2.0") 
 Please ensure this reflects the current release. 
 Application-Name (eg. "Vortex") 
 Please keep this consistent across versions of your application. 
 This information will allow us to track usage of your application and inform you of any odd usage patterns which may be caused by a bug in the software. 
 Unacceptable Usage 
 The following describes a number of example scenarios where the API or data retrieved from the API are being used improperly. Applications accessing our services in a comparable way may be actively blocked from using our API.
 Fetching data en-masse with the intent to rehost this information on your own service (i.e. scraping).
 Storing user API keys on your own server and/or using them without the action being initiated by the user. 
 Using personal API keys for a public-facing application.
 Sending request metadata which is either blank or impersonates another application.

I have reached a daily or hourly limit / API requests have been consumed / Rate Limit Exceeded - What does this mean?
 What is rate limiting?
 As a security measure, we limit user requests to our public API to a reasonable limit.
 The limit is 20,000 requests per 24-hour period , and once that limit has been reached 500 requests per hour . 
 To put this into perspective, Vortex consumes 3 requests per mod download (Nexus Mod Manager currently consumes twice as many per mod download) meaning you could, in theory, download up to 6664 mods via Vortex (or 3332 via Nexus Mod Manager) before reaching the 20,000 request limit.
 After that, you will then be limited to 500 requests per hour (around 165 mod downloads per hour via Vortex). Once you reach this hourly limit, you will be presented with a warning message upon making your 501st request:
 Rate Limiting Error/Warning Message in Vortex
 Rate Limiting Error/Warning Message in Nexus Mod Manager
 Rate Limiting Error/Warning message in Mod Organiser
 Once you have reached your limit - that is both the 20,000 request limit per 24h as well as the hourly 500 requests limit - you will be unable to make any more requests (such as mod downloads, mod update queries etc.) for the designated time frame (within the same hour). Please note that this measure is in place to protect our server infrastructure and maintain our site's functionality for all our users.
 When you have been rate-limited you will then simply have to wait until you can make further requests to our API.
 I have been rate-limited and have not downloaded anywhere close to 3300 mods in 24 hours. What is going on?
 If you have been rate-limited, it is because you have exceeded our daily and hourly request limit. Note that mod downloads are just one way of making requests to our API. Other ways of making requests include e.g. querying mod updates or mod information via a mod manager or other applications referencing our API.
 Please ensure that your mod manager is up to date to rule out the possibility of outdated software erroneously making an extraordinary amount of requests, which would lead to you being rate-limited.
 When will my API limit reset?
 The daily quota resets for all users at 00:00 GMT each day. The hourly quota resets each hour (e.g. 01:00 GMT, 02:00 GMT, etc).
 How can I see my remaining API requests?
 This information is sent in the response header to every request made to the API. Depending on which application you are using, there may be a way to see this number. For Vortex users, you can download this extension which adds a widget to the dashboard showing your remaining requests and reset times.

Based on the search results, here's what I found regarding the Nexus Mods API and download functionality:

Download link generation for a file requires different access depending on user status—if the user isn't premium on Nexus Mods, this requires a key that can only be generated on the website.

The Nexus Mods API Swagger documentation is available at https://app.swaggerhub.com/apis-docs/NexusMods/nexus-mods_public_api_params_in_form_d (the URL appears to be truncated in the search results), and official Nexus Mods API documentation is hosted at api-docs.nexusmods.com.

Regarding the specific "download_link.json" endpoint and premium-only restrictions, the search results confirm that premium status affects download link generation, but the detailed API specification for that specific endpoint is not clearly documented in these results. You may want to check the official API documentation sites directly for complete endpoint specifications.

## Search Results Summary

CurseForge uses the link style `https://mediafilez.forgecdn.net/files/[FILE ID]/[FULL FILE NAME]` as their media content delivery link.

The important detail regarding the "leading zero" and "4 digits" edge case is: The file id is segmented every four digits from left to right by a `/`.

This means when constructing the mediafilez URL, the file ID needs to be split into 4-digit segments separated by forward slashes. For example:
- A file ID like `1234567890` would be formatted as `1234/5678/90` in the URL path
- A file ID like `123` would need to be padded with leading zeros to `0000/0123` to maintain the 4-digit segmentation

This is the edge case you're referring to—when file IDs have fewer than 4 digits or don't divide evenly by 4, proper zero-padding with leading zeros becomes necessary to construct the correct mediafilez download URL.

content.text:
I've completed the research. Findings below. --- # PART 1 — CurseForge ("Eternal") API ## (a) Base URL, auth, keys, gates **Base URL** — verbatim from the docs: *"All endpoints use the same base URL - `https://api.curseforge.com`"* ([docs.curseforge.com/rest-api](https://docs.curseforge.com/rest-api/)) **Auth header** — verbatim: *"API Key (API_KEY) — Parameter Name: `x-api-key`, in: header. The API key can be generated in the CurseForge for Studios developer console."* (same page). Every endpoint ends with *"To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods: API_KEY"*. **How to get a key** — [console.curseforge.com](https://console.curseforge.com/) (SPA; I could only confirm it loads, not walk its UI). The gating is described verbatim in the support article ([support.curseforge.com/.../9000208346](https://support.curseforge.com/support/solutions/articles/9000208346-about-the-curseforge-api-and-how-to-apply-for-a-key), modified 3 Dec 2024): > "We're going to use the commonly used API system, which means API access will be granted to each requester as a unique key which can be generated after 3rd party developers submit an application. This can be done through a form and reviewed by the Overwolf team. The form covers contact information, project description, links and coursed, expected API use etc. To complete the form also requires approving the 3rd Party Developers API Terms of Service. Upon Overwolf review and approval, the unique key will be generated and the developer will be contacted via email." And the review criteria, verbatim: > "What will our team look for in the application? — How it impacts on Authors' earnings / How it affects CurseForge's servers and CDN / How it takes Authors' consent when it comes to third party distribution of their creations" **Is it free?** No price is stated anywhere I could find. But the 3rd Party API Terms contain a commercial trigger, verbatim: > "Upon the External App exceeding a certain quota, to be decided and updated from time to time upon Overwolf's sole discretion, continued use of the Platform API and/or SDK may (at Overwolf's sole discretion) require Developer to enter into a written licensing agreement with Overwolf, which license agreement may contain payment requirements or other terms and conditions applicable to the continued use of the API or SDK." ([3rd Party API T&C](https://support.curseforge.com/support/solutions/articles/9000207405-curseforge-3rd-party-api-terms-and-conditions)) **Could not verify:** an earlier automated read of the docs quoted *"Not a game developer? If you're running a 3rd party modding service, we have an API solution for you"* and *"Any registered account which is not a game developer and did not request a key, will be deleted."* I downloaded the raw HTML of `docs.curseforge.com/rest-api/` (1.1 MB) and **neither string is present**. Treat those as stale/unverified. **Keys are game-scoped.** `GET /v1/games` is documented as *"Get all games that are available to the provided API key."* — relevant to 403s (see (e)). ## (b) Core endpoints Full path inventory extracted from the rendered docs. **Three corrections to your list:** | Endpoint | Notes | |---|---| | `GET /v1/games` | params: `index`, `pageSize` | | `GET /v1/games/{gameId}`, `/versions`, `/version-types` | plus `GET /v2/games/{gameId}/versions` | | `GET /v1/categories` | `gameId` (**required**), `classId`, `classesOnly` | | `GET /v1/mods/search` | see below | | `GET /v1/mods/{modId}` | | | `POST /v1/mods` | *"Get a list of mods belonging the the same game."* Body: `{"modIds":[…],"filterPcOnly":true}` — **"mod ids must belong to the same game"** | | `POST /v1/mods/featured` | | | `GET /v1/mods/{modId}/description` | *"Get the full description of a mod in HTML format."* Params: `raw`, `stripped`, `markup` (all boolean) | | `GET /v1/mods/{modId}/files` | `gameVersion`, `modLoaderType`, `gameVersionTypeId`, `index`, `pageSize` | | `GET /v1/mods/{modId}/files/{fileId}` | | | `POST /v1/mods/files` | bulk by fileIds | | `GET /v1/mods/{modId}/files/{fileId}/changelog` | | | `GET /v1/mods/{modId}/files/{fileId}/download-url` | *"Get a download url for a specific file."* Returns `{"data":"string"}` | | **`POST` /v1/fingerprints** and **`POST` /v1/fingerprints/{gameId}**, `POST /v1/fingerprints/fuzzy`, `POST /v1/fingerprints/fuzzy/{gameId}` | ⚠️ **correction: there is no `GET /v1/fingerprints`** — fingerprint matching is POST-only, body `{"fingerprints":[…]}` | | **`GET /v1/minecraft/version`** and `/version/{gameVersionString}` | ⚠️ **correction: singular `version`, not `versions`** (the nav label says "Get Minecraft Versions" but the path is `/v1/minecraft/version`). Param `sortDescending` | | **`GET /v1/minecraft/modloader`** and `/modloader/{modLoaderName}` | ⚠️ singular. Params `version`, `includeAll` | **`GET /v1/mods/search` params** (verbatim from the table): `gameId` (**required**), `classId`, `categoryId`, `categoryIds`, `gameVersion`, `gameVersions`, `searchFilter`, `sortField`, `sortOrder`, `modLoaderType`, `modLoaderTypes`, `gameVersionTypeId`, `authorId`, `primaryAuthorId`, `slug`, `index`, `pageSize`. - `searchFilter`: *"Filter by free text search in the mod name and author"* - `slug`: *"Filter by slug (coupled with classId will result in a unique result)."* - Array caps: `categoryIds` max 10; `gameVersions` max 4; `modLoaderTypes` max 5. - `sortField` enum: `1=Featured, 2=Popularity, 3=LastUpdated, 4=Name, 5=Author, 6=TotalDownloads, 7=Category, 8=GameVersion, 9=EarlyAccess, 10=FeaturedReleased, 11=ReleasedDate, 12=Rating` - `modLoaderType` enum: `0=Any, 1=Forge, 2=Cauldron, 3=LiteLoader, 4=Fabric, 5=Quilt, 6=NeoForge`. Docs: *"Must be coupled with gameVersion."* **Pagination cap** — verbatim: > "Pagination Limits — The maximum page size is 50 results per page and capped at 10000 total results. Note: The limit is (index + pageSize <= 10,000)." This is a hard wall: you cannot page past 10,000 results for any query. To enumerate a full catalog you must shard queries (by `categoryId`, `gameVersion`, `modLoaderType`, `sortField`) so each slice stays under 10k. ## (c) Mod object fields — and the license question Complete `Mod` schema with the docs' own descriptions: `id`, `gameId`, `name`, `slug`, `links` (`ModLinks`: `websiteUrl`, `wikiUrl`, `issuesUrl`, `sourceUrl` — *"Relevant links for the mod such as Issue tracker and Wiki"*), `summary`, `status` (`ModStatus`: `1=New, 2=ChangesRequired, 3=UnderSoftReview, 4=Approved, 5=Rejected, 6=ChangesMade, 7=Inactive, 8=Abandoned, 9=Deleted, 10=UnderReview`), `downloadCount` (int64), `isFeatured`, `primaryCategoryId`, `categories[]`, `classId` (nullable), `authors[]` (`ModAuthor`: `id`, `name`, `url`), `logo` (`ModAsset`: `id`, `modId`, `title`, `description`, `thumbnailUrl`, `url`), `screenshots[]` (same `ModAsset` shape), `mainFileId`, `latestFiles[]` (full `File` objects), `latestFilesIndexes[]`, `latestEarlyAccessFilesIndexes[]`, `dateCreated`, `dateModified`, `dateReleased`, `allowModDistribution` (`boolean¦null` — *"Is mod allowed to be distributed"*), `gamePopularityRank`, `isAvailable` (*"Is the mod available for search. This can be false when a mod is experimental, in a deleted state or has only alpha files"*), `thumbsUpCount`, `rating` (nullable decimal). `File` object: `id`, `gameId`, `modId`, `isAvailable` (*"Whether the file is available to download"*), `displayName`, `fileName`, `releaseType`, `fileStatus`, `hashes[]` (md5/sha1), `fileDate`, `fileLength`, `downloadCount`, `fileSizeOnDisk`, **`downloadUrl`** (*"The file download URL"*), `gameVersions[]`, `sortableGameVersions[]`, `dependencies[]` (`modId` + `relationType`), `exposeAsAlternative`, `parentProjectFileId`, `alternateFileId`, **`isServerPack`**, **`serverPackFileId`**, `isEarlyAccessContent`, `earlyAccessEndDate`, `fileFingerprint`, `modules[]`. > `isServerPack` / `serverPackFileId` are the two fields that matter most for a hosting installer — many Minecraft modpacks ship a distinct server-side pack file. ### License: confirmed — **the CurseForge API does NOT expose a license field.** ✅ I grepped the entire rendered docs page (211 KB of text, every schema and every example response). The word "license" appears exactly **4 times**, all inside the *CurseForge for Studios Terms of Use* legal boilerplate ("non-exclusive, royalty-free, worldwide license to the name, logo and trademarks…"). It appears in **zero** schema definitions. There is no `license`, `licenseType`, `licenseUrl`, or `licenseName` on `Mod`, `File`, or any other object. Corroborating evidence: [cfwidget.com](https://cfwidget.com/), the long-standing third-party CurseForge proxy, still has a `license` key in its JSON but it is **empty for every project I tested** — JEI, JourneyMap, Applied Energistics 2, Iron Chests, Create all return `"license": ""` (tested live against `api.cfwidget.com`). **Where license lives instead:** on the CurseForge *website*, on the project's **License tab** (author-editable) and rendered in the project page's About panel. The support article on the distribution toggle says, verbatim: *"Simply click the 'Go to License Tab' button and you'll be transferred to the relevant tab… You can also edit this toggle by entering the project page > 'License tab'."* and *"Only project owners and members with the 'license' permission enabled can view the License tab"* ([Project Distribution Toggle](https://support.curseforge.com/support/solutions/articles/9000207877-project-distribution-toggle)). **Practical consequence for you:** you cannot build a license-filtered catalog from the API. Getting license text means scraping `www.curseforge.com` — which is **explicitly prohibited** (see (g)) and technically blocked (I got `HTTP 403 "Just a moment… Enable JavaScript and cookies to continue"` — Cloudflare challenge — on both `curseforge.com/legal/terms` and `curseforge.com/terms/mod-author` from this server). ## (d) The `allowModDistribution=false` / `downloadUrl=null` problem **What it is.** Authors can flip a per-project switch. Verbatim from CurseForge ([Project Distribution Toggle](https://support.curseforge.com/support/solutions/articles/9000207877-project-distribution-toggle)): > "The project distribution toggle is all about providing authors control over their intellectual property and revenue generated from their awesome creations. The toggle is part of the new CurseForge API, and determines if 3rd party developers can or cannot distribute your project information and files." > > "If you turn this option off **Any 3rd-party service, website or client will not have access to your projects or files via the 3rd-party API.**" > > "If you turn this option on any download from the 3rd party service **will not count towards your total downloads nor towards your Reward Program earnings.**" > > "As a default, all existing projects have the option toggled on and allow distribution." > > **"We recommend choosing a license preference that is compatible with your distribution choice. In any case - the API will respect the toggle choice over the license type choice."** That last sentence is the one to internalise: **an MIT- or LGPL-licensed mod can still have `allowModDistribution=false`, and CurseForge will enforce the toggle over the licence.** The open licence may give you the legal right to redistribute, but CurseForge will not serve you the bytes through the API. **Mechanically**, `Mod.allowModDistribution=false` ⇒ `File.downloadUrl` comes back `null` and `/download-url` fails. The API returns full metadata but no file. **How widespread?** No official statistic exists — I searched and could not find one, and CurseForge has never published a number. Only anecdotes, and they cut both ways: - All the Mods 9 (a ~400-mod pack): 3 mods blocked. - A 114-mod pack: 4 blocked ([xenodeve/minecraft-100day#80](https://github.com/xenodeve/minecraft-100day/issues/80)). - Individual high-traffic libraries have been the pain point — e.g. long-running author requests on [architectury/architectury-api#262](https://github.com/architectury/architectury-api/issues/262), [EccentricVamp/EccentricTome#18](https://github.com/EccentricVamp/EccentricTome/issues/18), [Flemmli97/TenshiLib#8](https://github.com/Flemmli97/TenshiLib/issues/8), [mrsterner/GuardVillagers#23](https://github.com/mrsterner/GuardVillagers/issues/23), [r8420/MoreOverlays-updated#62](https://github.com/r8420/MoreOverlays-updated/issues/62). **Realistic read: low single-digit percent of projects, but non-uniformly distributed** — it clusters on libraries and popular mods, so the probability that *a given modpack* contains at least one blocked mod is high. For your use case that is what matters: a 1–3% per-mod block rate is a ~50%+ per-pack failure rate. **What third-party launchers actually do — they all give up and hand it to the human:** - **Prism Launcher**: on a blocked mod the pack install halts and the user is given a link list; Prism then watches the Downloads folder and copies files into place. Tracked as bugs because the UX is bad: [#599 "Attempting to download mods from CurseForge that have 3rd party downloads disabled results in undetermined behavior"](https://github.com/PrismLauncher/PrismLauncher/issues/599) (version dropdown shows *"No valid version found!"*; downloads fail silently and the mod appears installed but isn't), [#3220](https://github.com/PrismLauncher/PrismLauncher/issues/3220), [#3844](https://github.com/PrismLauncher/PrismLauncher/issues/3844). - **itzg/docker-minecraft-server** (the de-facto standard Minecraft server image, i.e. your closest analogue): verbatim from its docs — *"For mod, modpacks, and world files that are not allowed for automated download, the container path `/downloads` can be attached and matching files will be retrieved from there."* and *"It's important to use a browser to download the files listed for manual download."* ([auto-curseforge docs](https://docker-minecraft-server.readthedocs.io/en/latest/types-and-platforms/mod-platforms/auto-curseforge/)) - **Modrinth** deliberately does not integrate: *"some of them, like CurseForge, are Modrinth's competitors. They won't allow the use of their APIs to Modrinth, or if they do, it would be under a contract with terms that might make experience worse for Modrinth users."* ([modrinth/code#3631](https://github.com/modrinth/code/issues/3631)) **What it means for a hosting company.** You cannot promise "one-click install for any CurseForge mod." You must: 1. Store `allowModDistribution` per mod, refresh it (authors flip it), and **exclude or clearly badge blocked mods in your catalog UI** rather than failing at install time. 2. Provide an upload/SFTP fallback path for blocked mods — that is what every serious tool does, and it is also the honest answer to give customers. 3. Never construct a CDN URL to bypass the flag. Doing so circumvents an access-control mechanism, which is a named prohibited act in the API terms (see (g)) and voids the author consent that CurseForge's whole approval process is built around. **Historical context**: the toggle shipped alongside the official API on 16 May 2022, which broke MultiMC/PolyMC/GDLauncher/PCL2 modpack installs. CurseForge's rationale, as reported: downloads from 3rd-party services rely on CurseForge servers and CDN, incurring costs and bypassing the monetization that funds the Author Rewards program. ## (e) CDN URL pattern, manual construction, and your 403 — **I reproduced this live** ### The URL scheme (empirically verified today from this server) `edge.forgecdn.net` is a CloudFront distribution that **302-redirects** to `mediafilez.forgecdn.net` (Fastly/ioRiver in front of an S3 bucket). Observed: ``` GET https://edge.forgecdn.net/files/8911/160/jei-26.3-neoforge-31.0.0.7.jar → HTTP/2 302, location: https://mediafilez.forgecdn.net/files/8911/160/... (via CloudFront, x-amz-cf-pop: SIN3-P4) → HTTP/2 200, 1,905,807 bytes, content-type: application/java-archive (server: AmazonS3, x-ioriver: Fastly) ``` **The exact fileId → path rule (I tested all four variants):** ``` https://mediafilez.forgecdn.net/files/{floor(fileId/1000)}/{fileId % 1000}/{fileName} ``` | Tested path | Result | |---|---| | `/files/8911/160/jei-26.3-neoforge-31.0.0.7.jar` (id 8911160) | **200**, 1905807 B | | `/files/8880/75/jei-26.2-neoforge-30.32.0.220.jar` (id 8880**075**) | **200**, 1919971 B | | `/files/8880/**075**/…` (zero-padded) | **403** | | `/files/8851/9/jei-1.20.1-forge-15.59.0.210.jar` (id 8851**009**) | **200**, 1825651 B | | `/files/8851/**009**/…` (zero-padded) | **403** | ⚠️ **The second segment is NOT zero-padded.** This is the classic bug: fileId `8851009` → `8851/9`, not `8851/009`. Padding gives a 403. (Note the community shorthand *"the file id is segmented every four digits"* from [Coadon/CurseFetch](https://github.com/Coadon/CurseFetch) is a rough approximation that breaks on these cases — use `divmod(fileId, 1000)`.) ### Your 403 with empty body — diagnosed **It is almost certainly `api.curseforge.com`, not the CDN.** I reproduced it exactly: ``` $ curl -D - https://api.curseforge.com/v1/games # no key HTTP/2 403 content-length: 0 x-cache: Error from cloudfront $ curl -H "x-api-key: notarealkey" https://api.curseforge.com/v1/games HTTP/2 403 (empty body) ``` **403 + `content-length: 0` + `x-cache: Error from cloudfront` is CloudFront rejecting the API key at the edge before your request reaches the app.** Causes, in order of likelihood: 1. **Key mangled by shell/env interpolation.** CurseForge keys are bcrypt-shaped (`$2a$10$…`). `$2a`, `$10` get eaten by shell `$`-expansion / Docker Compose variable substitution, silently truncating the key. This is by far the most-reported cause: [itzg/docker-minecraft-server#3591 "Access to CurseForge API is forbidden despite valid CF_API_KEY"](https://github.com/itzg/docker-minecraft-server/issues/3591) — the fix is no quotes in `.env`, or `$$` doubling in Compose. Check the key's exact byte length at the point of use. 2. **Key not authorised for that game.** Docs: *"Get all games that are available to the provided API key."* Keys are scoped; a Studios/game-developer key will 403 on Minecraft data. 3. **Rate limited.** When throttled, CloudFront returns a **403 with an HTML body** (not empty): `ERROR: The request could not be satisfied …

403 ERROR

Users found in violation of this term may have their account suspended.**" **§11 "No text or data mining, or web scraping"** — verbatim: > "**You shall not conduct, facilitate, authorise or permit any text or data mining or web scraping in relation to our site or any services provided via, or in relation to, our site for any purpose.** This includes using (or permitting, authorising or attempting the use of): > - **Any 'robot', 'bot', 'spider', 'scraper' or other automated device, program, tool, algorithm, code, process or methodology to access, obtain, copy, monitor or republish any portion of our site or any data, content, information or services accessed via the same.** > - Any automated analytical technique aimed at analysing text and data in digital form to generate information or develop, train, fine-tune or validate AI systems or models… > > The provisions in this clause should be treated as an express reservation of our rights in this regard, including for the purposes of Article 4(3) of the Digital Copyright Directive ((EU) 2019/790)." **§24 "Rights you are giving us and others to use material you upload"** — the licence mod authors grant, verbatim: > "you grant such users a worldwide, non-exclusive, royalty-free, transferable licence for to download and use the content **for their own recreational purposes** and, **where permitted by you at the time of upload**, for the purposes of distributing content and/or a modified or enhanced reproduction of the content." Note: the licence to *distribute* is opt-in per upload, and the base grant is limited to *"own recreational purposes"* — not commercial hosting. **§27 "Rules about linking to our site"** — verbatim: *"You may link to our home page, provided you do so in a way that is fair and legal… You must not establish a link in such a way as to suggest any form of association, approval or endorsement on our part where none exists."* and *"If you wish to link to or make any use of content on our site other than that set out above, please contact support@nexusmods.com."* **§28**, verbatim: *"Please note that we only provide our site for domestic and private use. You agree not to use our site for any commercial or business purposes…"* (This sits in the consumer-liability section, so its force is contextual — but it reinforces the §10 commercial-use prohibition.) Also relevant to a hosting business carrying third-party mod content — verbatim, appearing three times in the ToS: > "**Third parties who use our APIs are responsible for filtering the content returned.**" i.e. adult/age-restricted content filtering is **your** legal obligation, not Nexus's. ## (f) Practical verdict on Nexus — **NO. Unambiguously no.** Nexus Mods is **not usable** as a source for a commercial hosting platform's auto-installer. This is not a grey area; it fails on four independent grounds, each individually disqualifying, and each stated in Nexus's own words: 1. **The installer itself is a named prohibited use.** — *"Storing user API keys on your own server and/or using them without the action being initiated by the user."* ([AUP](https://help.nexusmods.com/article/114-api-acceptable-use-policy)) A server-side auto-installer is exactly this. 2. **The catalog itself is a named prohibited use.** — *"Fetching data en-masse with the intent to rehost this information on your own service (i.e. scraping)."* ([AUP](https://help.nexusmods.com/article/114-api-acceptable-use-policy)) Reinforced by ToS §11: *"You shall not conduct, facilitate, authorise or permit any text or data mining or web scraping… for any purpose."* 3. **Commercial use requires a licence you don't have.** — *"You must not use any part of the content on our site for commercial purposes without obtaining a licence to do so from us or our licensors."* (ToS §10) And downloads are permitted *"for your own personal use"* only. 4. **The download mechanism is deliberately engineered to prevent it.** — *"This ensures that all non-premium members must access the website to download through the API"*, backed by `403: "You don't have permission to get download links from the API without visting nexusmods.com - this is for premium users only."* ([v1 spec](https://app.swaggerhub.com/apis-docs/NexusMods/nexus-mods_public_api_params_in_form_data/1.0)) Plus per-user rate limits that make *your* traffic exhaust *your customer's* quota. There is no "ask nicely and get a licence" path worth pursuing here either: registration is discretionary (*"We reserve the right to deny registration… with or without providing a reason"*), favours open-source apps, and the whole policy is framed around *"the benefit of the modding community"* rather than commercial resale. **Recommendation:** drop Nexus from the auto-installer scope entirely. If you want to serve Nexus-modded games (Skyrim, Fallout, Stardew, Valheim, etc.), the only defensible design is **link-out plus customer upload**: deep-link the customer to the mod page on nexusmods.com (permitted under §27 if you don't imply endorsement), let them download it themselves under their own account and licence, and give them a clean SFTP/web-upload path into their server. That keeps the download "initiated by the user", under the user's own account, at the user's own quota — and it is honest with the customer about where the file came from. --- # Cross-cutting recommendations **CurseForge is the viable source — conditionally.** Modrinth (not researched here, but the obvious third leg) is the genuinely permissive option and should be your primary; CurseForge second, with an approved key; Nexus link-out only. **Before writing installer code, get three things in writing from Overwolf** as part of the key application — all three are real blockers, not formalities: 1. **Permission to cache API data.** The literal terms say *"save or cache any data obtained through the API or SDK"* is prohibited. Your catalog cannot exist without caching. Ask explicitly. 2. **Confirmation you are not a "competitor."** *"shall not… build any product or service that competes, directly or indirectly, with CF, CurseForge for Studios, or the Platform."* A hosting company shipping a mod browser is arguable. Get it acknowledged. 3. **A rate-limit/quota figure.** Nothing is published; the terms let Overwolf impose a paid licensing agreement above an undisclosed quota. Ask what the quota is before you build capacity assumptions on it. **Three engineering constraints to design around from day one:** - **Persist and refresh `allowModDistribution`**; badge or hide blocked mods in the catalog rather than failing at install. Ship the manual-upload fallback in v1, not v2 — every comparable tool needed it. - **Add `x-api-key` to CDN fetches now.** Enforcement was announced for 2026-07-16 and has slipped, but it will land, and the failure mode is a hard 401 on every install. - **Build your own throttle.** CurseForge returns no rate-limit headers; a 403 with an HTML body means throttled, a 403 with an empty body means bad key. Catalog sync must be a sharded, resumable background job — the 10,000-result pagination cap means you cannot enumerate any large category in one pass. **Fix the current 403 first** — check the API key's byte length at the point of use. Bcrypt-shaped keys (`$2a$10$…`) get silently truncated by shell and Docker Compose `$`-expansion, and that single cause accounts for most reported CurseForge 403s. **Two things I could not verify:** whether CurseForge keys carry any monetary cost at the tier you'd need (no pricing is published anywhere; the terms only say a written licensing agreement "may contain payment requirements" above an undisclosed quota), and the current console.curseforge.com signup flow (it's a JS app I couldn't drive). Both need a human to walk the console and the application form.
